notes: Comments: select some words and choose Comment (✎) in the toolbar, or press Ctrl+Alt+M, to leave a note on them. A chapter's details list its comments, and Review has a Comments section for the whole book.
Resolve a comment once it's dealt with: it stays with its words, unhighlighted, and can be reopened. Comments never appear in the PDF or EPUB.
The "preview" notes are gone from the About box, Settings, Typesetting and Publishing, which now say what the Studio includes.
Maintenance release, with screenshots of the Studio in NorthRay Launcher and on the website.
Settings are read more carefully: a setting saved by another version can no longer stop the Studio starting.
Maintenance release.

Review (new): compare any chapter or scene with an earlier version or a snapshot. Added words are shaded and removed words struck through, with counts, and you can restore the older text (the current one is kept, so it can be undone).
Snapshots: save the whole book as it is (before a revision, before sending it to an editor) and see later which chapters changed and by how much. Snapshots are kept until you remove them.

Names: a continuity check finds spellings close to a name in the world's bible (“Marren” for “Maren”) and names used often that aren't in it yet. Add one as another name, add it to the bible, or mark it as fine.
Goals: set a daily word goal and see today's words, the last 7 and 28 days, your streak, and a chart of each day. Writing's status bar shows today's progress.
Libraries are upgraded automatically.

Planning (new): the Planning tab shows every chapter and scene as a card on a board, in the order of the book and grouped by part. Each card shows its status (with a coloured edge), synopsis, viewpoint character, and words against its target.
Cards show which characters appear in each chapter and scene, found in the text from the world's bible.
Word targets for the book and for each chapter or scene, with progress in the sidebar and on the cards. Filter the board by status: outline, draft, revised or final.
Choose a chapter's or scene's viewpoint character from the world's characters. The panel lists every entry that appears in it, linked to Worldbuilding.
Move cards earlier or later, add chapters and scenes, and open any of them in Writing. Libraries are upgraded automatically.
Worldbuilding (new): every world keeps a bible of characters, places, groups, things, lore and events, shared by all its books. Independent books get their own.
Each entry has other names it goes by, a summary, a picture, a list of details (Age: 34, Eyes: grey), and notes.
Relationships between entries read correctly from both sides: “Lives in Highcliff” on a character shows as “Home of” on the place.
Appears in: each entry lists the chapters and scenes its name (or another name it goes by) appears in, with how often and the first time in context. Click one to open it in Writing.
A world's page in the Library summarises its entries. Entries go to the Trash and can be restored.

Editions (new): each book can have a paperback, hardback, large-print and ebook edition, each with its own ISBN. Print editions can have their own trim size and design; a new large-print edition starts with the large-print design.
Publishing works one edition at a time: print editions get their checks, spine and cover measurements, a print-ready PDF and a proof; the ebook edition gets the EPUB.
The copyright page, in print and in the EPUB, lists every edition's ISBN.
Checks fit the edition: no print checks for the ebook, no ebook cover check for print, and a warning if two editions share an ISBN.
Existing books get a paperback (with the book's ISBN and its publishing settings) and an ebook edition the first time Publishing opens them. Libraries are upgraded automatically.
Publishing (new): the Publishing tab checks the book, gives the measurements for its cover, and makes the files for printers and ebook stores.

Print-ready PDF in the PDF/X-1a format print-on-demand printers ask for: text in pure black, pictures in grey (or CMYK for a colour interior), fonts embedded, and an optional 0.125-inch bleed on the outside edges.

EPUB 3 ebook export, with an EPUB 2 contents file for older readers: cover, title and copyright pages, a contents list with parts and chapters, pictures cropped and sized for e-readers, and accessibility information. It uses the same chapters as the Preview.
Pre-flight checks: missing author, description or cover; an ISBN with a wrong check digit; pictures without a description, or that would print blurred; too few pages for a paperback.
Spine width for white or cream paper, and the full cover size with bleed, for your cover designer. Check them against your printer's own cover template before the cover is finished.

Preview (new): see the book as an ebook on a phone, a 6-inch e-ink reader or a tablet. Turn pages by clicking or with the arrow keys, and try the reader's own settings: white, sepia or night pages, text size, and the book's typeface, a serif or a sans-serif.
Typesetting: zoom (fit, actual size, 200%), single pages as well as spreads, and guides showing the margins, the baseline grid and the spine edge.
Typesetting: chapter openings with “Chapter One” above the title, or a large numeral; drop caps; front matter numbered i, ii, iii, with the story starting at page 1 on a right-hand page.
Chapters already titled “Chapter 3: …” keep their number; prologues, acknowledgements and the like aren't numbered.
Typesetting: a contents page with page numbers (parts in small capitals, chapters indented).
Typesetting: a copyright page on the back of the title page, made only from the book's own details (author, edition, ISBN); with none of those it stays blank.
Typesetting: chapters can open with their first words in small capitals.
Typesetting: margin controls (inside, outside, top and bottom).
Exported PDFs are much smaller: only the letters used are embedded.
PDF import: a title page in large type stays front matter instead of becoming chapters; “CHAPTER ONE” joins the title on the line below it; placeholder details such as “unspecified” are ignored.
Typesetting (new): the Typesetting tab sets your whole book as printed pages and shows them as two-page spreads. Text is justified and hyphenated, with real kerning, ligatures and small capitals.
Paragraphs are set as a whole (the Knuth–Plass method TeX uses), so spacing stays even. Widows and orphans are prevented, and chapters open part-way down a new page.
Pages include a title page, part pages, running heads (book title on the left, chapter on the right), page numbers, scene breaks, and your pictures with their crops and captions.

Four starting designs (Classic, Open, Ragged right, Large print), plus typeface, type size, line spacing, trim size, justified or ragged text, hyphenation, chapters on right-hand pages, running heads and title page. Each book remembers its design.
Export the typeset book as a PDF with the fonts embedded and text that can be searched and copied. Print-ready PDF/X for printers comes with publishing.
Bundled book fonts: Crimson Text and Gentium Book (SIL Open Font License). British and US English hyphenation.

Artwork library: a new Artwork page lists every picture in your library, stored once however many chapters use it. Add pictures, name them, mark them as a map, illustration, ornament and so on, and see which chapters use each one.
Pictures in the text can be cropped, sized and aligned from the details panel: drag the frame or its corners to crop. The stored picture is never changed, so a crop can always be undone.
Print checks: each picture shows its printed size and resolution for the book's trim size, with a warning below 300 ppi and a stronger one below 150, and a one-click size that prints sharply.
Books have a trim size (6 × 9 in, A5, B-format and more), and measurements can be shown in inches, centimetres, millimetres or pixels (Settings).
New pictures start at the widest size that prints sharply. Pictures that came with imported books are listed in the artwork library too.
+ Scene now adds a *** divider at the end of the chapter, with the cursor ready for the new scene, instead of a separate page.
Captions and screen-reader descriptions for pictures.

No more Windows menu bar: every command has a place in the window. A new Settings page (in the top bar, or Ctrl+,) holds the library folder, export and backup, the theme and a full list of keyboard shortcuts; New book and Import sit on the Library page; Move to Trash is in the details panel; the editor toolbar has previous and next chapter buttons.
Ctrl+Up and Ctrl+Down move to the previous or next chapter, from the text or the outline.
Saving... then Saved, in the editor and the status bar, so you can see your words are stored.
The Studio reopens the book and chapter you were working on.
Double-click a book to open it in Writing. New chapters, scenes and parts start with their title selected; press Enter to go straight to the text.
An empty chapter shows a faint prompt; a new library offers Create a book and Import a book.
One details panel layout for books, chapters and scenes, in tidy sections; the outline lines up with the Library sidebar.
The import preview fits the window, and switching chapters no longer flickers.
No scroll bars anywhere, including the longer text boxes; the wheel and keys still scroll.

Word (.docx) and OpenDocument (.odt) import: chapters from heading styles (or from lines like "CHAPTER ONE" when there are none), parts, italic, bold, small caps, quotes, lists, pictures, links, footnotes (gathered into Notes) and the document's title and author. Tracked changes come in as accepted.
Fixed: some documents' formatting was ignored when it was set through their styles.
Smoother animations: eased page changes, status messages that fade in and out, and softer hover effects.
Book covers lift slightly on hover; the workspace tabs, sidebar and outline highlights slide to your choice; the import tick boxes animate.
The Bookshelf/List switch no longer overlaps the filter button.
Fixes the Studio closing while importing: files are now read by a separate helper process, so a file the importer can't handle shows an explanation instead of closing the app.
Unexpected errors while reading or importing are explained rather than closing the app.
If the Studio ever does close unexpectedly, it notes where in crash.log (in %LOCALAPPDATA%\NorthRay\Writing Studio) so the cause can be found.
The Writing workspace: parts, chapters and scenes in an outline you can drag to rearrange, with word counts and a status for each.

A page-like editor with paragraph styles (Body, First paragraph, Centred, Epigraph, Attribution, Verse, Letter, Note, headings), bold, italic, underline, small caps, scene breaks, quotes, lists and pictures.
Saves as you type; keeps an earlier version of each chapter and scene every ten minutes or so (the last 40), which you can restore.

Import from EPUB (parts, chapters, front and back matter, styling, pictures, title, author and cover), HTML, Markdown and plain text, with a preview to choose what comes in. DRM-protected books are refused.
PDF import (experimental): chapters and paragraphs are worked out from the page layout, so check the result.
Subtle animations throughout, and hidden scroll bars.
First preview (Milestone 1): the Author Library.
Worlds, series and books, including standalone books and books outside any world.
Separate reading and chronological order for every series; drag and drop to reorder or move.
Covers, world banners and logos; details edited in a side panel that saves as you type.
A safe local library: every change saved at once, a backup each time it opens, the Trash, and JSON export.
